chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, both, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, who said:

I wrote to him, meaning Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him), while I was in Medina in the year two hundred and thirty-one: 'May I be sacrificed for you! A man instructed a man to buy goods for him, or something else. So he bought it, but it was stolen from him, or the road was cut off for him (by a bandit). From whose wealth is the loss of the goods? Is it from the wealth of the one who instructed, or from the wealth of the one who was instructed?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'From the wealth of the one who instructed.'

key_terms.الآمِر: The principal or one who gives the order/instruction
key_terms.الْمَأْمُور: The agent or one who is instructed to act
key_terms.قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِ الطَّرِيق: The road was cut off (referring to banditry or loss during transit)

ai.seo_question: Who bears the financial loss if goods bought by an agent are stolen before delivery?
ai.summary: Recorded during the Minor Occultation, this hadith from Imam al-Hadi (AS) clarifies the principle of 'ghurm bi al-ghinm' (risk follows profit) in agency, ruling that the principal bears the loss if goods are lost before the agent takes possession. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the agent acts merely as a conduit for the principal's wealth until actual delivery, distinguishing it from other commercial risk models.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ja’far Abu Al Abbas Al Kufy, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany who said,

‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3<sup>rd</sup>, and I was in Al-Medina in the year two hundred and thirty one: ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! A man instructed a man to buy some goods for him, or other than that. So he bought it but it was stolen from him, or the road was cut-off upon him (by a bandit). From whose assets is this loss, it is from the assets of the one who asked to buy or the one who bought the goods?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘From the wealth of the instructor’.
en.sarwar: 43. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd Allah from ibn Mahbub from Sanaa ‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One who consumes the assets of a believing person in unlawful ways is not of my follower and friends.’”
